title: Refill issue51846 DDL owner topology handoff: owner epoch token must reject stale reorg result

payload.validation_scope: deterministic root-boundary replay of the ownerTS comparison used by runReorgJob; live cluster owner/PD topology handoff remains a higher-level lift
payload.red_signature: same TiDB retires and becomes DDL owner again within the same wall-clock second; previous reorg result ownerTS equals current ownerTS and would pass the stale-result filter
payload.green_signature: renewOwnerTS(max(wallTS, previous+1)) makes owner epoch tokens monotonic even when wall-clock seconds collide, so previous reorg result is rejected
payload.user_symptom: A long DDL reorg can accept a late result from a previous DDL owner epoch after a rapid owner retire/re-become cycle, potentially applying stale row count/progress/error into the new owner epoch instead of retrying as an owner handoff.
payload.next_step: lift this narrowed oracle to a controlled owner handoff testbed by forcing retire/re-become while a reorg worker is active and observing ownerTS mismatch/retry rather than accepting the stale doneCh result

provenance.source: current TiDB source inspection plus RED/GREEN local patch

name: DDL reorg owner epoch token must be unique across owner handoff

payload.p_check: runReorgJob records reorgCtx.getOwnerTS before launching the reorg function and later accepts the doneCh result when res.ownerTS equals the current ownerTS.
payload.q_claim: ownerTS equality proves the result belongs to the current DDL owner epoch on this TiDB instance.
payload.fault: OnBecomeOwner currently derives ownerTS from time.Now().Unix(); the same TiDB instance can retire and become owner again within one wall-clock second, so two different owner epochs can share one token.

boundary.before: a reorg function from owner epoch A is still running or sends a late doneCh result
boundary.fault: the same TiDB retires and becomes DDL owner again before the wall-clock second changes
boundary.after: runReorgJob compares res.ownerTS with reorgCtx.getOwnerTS and decides whether to accept the result or return a retry timeout

pkg/ddl/reorg.go runReorgJob stores beOwnerTS and sends it in reorgFnResult
pkg/ddl/reorg.go runReorgJob accepts doneCh result unless res.ownerTS != curTS
pkg/ddl/ddl.go reorgContexts stores the owner token as beOwnerTS
side_effects: stale previous-owner reorg result can be accepted by the new owner epoch
row count/progress/warnings or a reorg error can be applied in the wrong epoch
the intended topology-handoff retry path is skipped
consumers: ADD INDEX reorg/backfill paths using runReorgJob
other long DDL reorg operations that rely on doneCh ownerTS filtering

name: DDL stale reorg result is rejected after owner epoch changes

payload.contract: A reorgFnResult produced under a previous DDL owner epoch must not be accepted after the same TiDB has retired and become owner again, even if both owner transitions occur in the same wall-clock second.
minimal_observation: capture owner token for epoch A
simulate owner retire and re-become with the same wall-clock second input
RED if previousOwnerTS equals curOwnerTS because the stale result would pass runReorgJob's ownerTS equality check
GREEN if the renewed owner token differs from the previous token and the stale result is rejected

green_signature.fix_shape: renewOwnerTS sets ownerTS to wallTS or previous+1 when wallTS does not advance

blind_spots: Root-boundary replay does not prove that the exact same-second owner re-election is frequent in a live cluster
Root-boundary replay does not inspect final ADD INDEX state; the cluster lift should observe job state/logs around forced owner handoff
reusable_for: owner epoch tokens derived from coarse wall-clock time
async worker result filters that rely on equality with a mutable owner/session token
topology-fault schedules where old goroutines can overlap with new leadership
